thesis: DoorDash (Nasdaq: DASH). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-30) downloaded and read: statements, convertible note, credit facility, MD&A metrics. Q3 total orders 993M vs 776M (+28%), Marketplace GOV 33,941M vs 25,015M (+36%) including Deliveroo (acquired 2025-10-02, 3,724M consideration) so reported growth is partly acquired. 9M revenue 13,106M vs 9,762M (+34%); 9M NI 850M vs 722M. TTM (USD millions, FY25 10-K + 9M26 - 9M25): NI 1063 (935+850-722); OCF 2953 (2,431+2,532-2,010); PP&E capex 262 (257+208-203); capitalized software 488 (348+375-235); FCF 2203; SBC 1123 (1,051+847-775); FCF after SBC 1080. Close 166.8 (2026-11-18) x 435,976,331 shares (Class A 411,998,576 + Class B 23,977,755, 10-Q cover 2026-10-26; Class B converts 1:1, assumption) = 72.7B = 68x TTM NI; FCF yield 3.0% (1.5% after SBC). Cash 5,053M + short term investments 929M = 5,982M vs 0% convertible notes 2,728M carrying (2,750M principal due 2030-05-15): net cash about 3,254M, before merchant and Dasher payables inside 5,645M accrued liabilities. Price implies sustained 25%+ GOV growth and large margin expansion; the filing shows growth and net cash but earnings are small relative to price. Stock fell 5.8% on 2026-11-19 (157.21 stockanalysis.com, 157.13 Yahoo; cause not investigated).
counterthesis: Valuation: 68x GAAP earnings and FCF yield 1.5% after SBC; SBC is about 38% of OCF and annual dilution is real (Class A shares +2.3M in 9M after buybacks unread). Reported growth is boosted by Deliveroo; organic growth not separated. 9M NI rose only 18% against 34% revenue growth, so margin leverage is not evident in GAAP; accrued liabilities 5,645M mean OCF benefits from merchant payable timing. Competition (Uber Eats, Instacart, Amazon), regulation of gig workers and fees, and heavy investment in autonomous delivery and international expansion are not quantified. Peers, own history, goodwill 5.5B impairment risk, legal notes and 8-K release unread.
invalidation: Invalidated if organic order growth drops below about 15%, if GAAP operating margin does not expand while revenue grows 30%, if SBC plus buybacks do not offset dilution, or if regulatory changes raise Dasher cost materially.
